tonight.headline: Nothing has kicked off, and the only clock running tonight is Stafford's.
body: Your 77% is not a read on your roster, it is a read on theirs. KEI returns have five starters set and four slots empty — both wide receiver spots, the kicker and the defence — with Drake London, George Pickens, Parker Washington, Jalen Coker, the 49ers defence and Evan McPherson all sitting on their bench. That has been true for three days. Their projected 70.8 against your 121.1 is mostly the four zeroes.

Do not plan around it. If they set that lineup before Sunday morning they add roughly fifty points and the matchup is a coin flip. The one thing in this brief you can actually act on tonight is below, and it expires at 01:00.

case.label: What the 77% is actually made of
case.body: Adding London 12.9, Pickens 14.8, McPherson 7.9 and the 49ers defence 7.4 to their lineup is 43.0 points of empty slot. Their filled five — Dart, Achane, Skattebo, Tyler Warren, Etienne — project 70.9, which is a competent core. The gap is administrative, not structural.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Any lineup activity from KEI returns before Sunday 11:00. Their last recorded transaction in the activity log is not a lineup move, so there is no evidence either way about whether they are paying attention this week.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Do NOT claim — he is free at 01:00 Saturday Mexico City
doFirst.title: At 01:00 tonight, add Matthew Stafford free — drop MarShawn Lloyd
doFirst.subtitle: Two hours and twenty-five minutes from now the price on the best available quarterback in this league drops from your entire season's waiver priority to nothing. This is the run before that happens.

case.label: The clock, in your time
case.body: His clearsAt is 07:00 UTC on 19 September, which is 01:00 Saturday in Mexico City. Until that moment he is on WAIVERS and the only way to get him is a CLAIM. IPADE priority never resets, you sit 3rd of 10, and one claim drops you to last for the rest of the season. Claiming him tonight would be the single most expensive move available on this roster. Waiting two hours costs nothing and gets the identical player.

case.label: Why he is worth a bench seat at all
case.body: Trevor Lawrence is your only quarterback and projects 14.9 with Jacksonville implied 21.0 at Denver. Stafford projects 17.4 with the Rams implied 27.75 — tied with Baltimore for the highest implied total on the Week 2 board — at home on Monday night against a Giants team implied 20.75. He is 90.5% rostered nationally and QB11. That is the ownership anomaly STRATEGY section 4 calls the strongest single wire signal in a shallow league, and here it costs a free agent transaction.

case.label: Checked tonight, not assumed
case.body: The Rams filed their Week 2 injury report for Monday Night Football today: Kam Curl, Omar Speights, Nate Landman, Kamren Kinchens and Davante Adams. Stafford is not on it. The falsification clause on file — 'Los Angeles put Stafford on an injury report before Monday night' — has not fired, and this is the last report before the deadline.

case.label: The drop, unsoftened
case.body: MarShawn Lloyd averaged 2.8 yards a carry in Week 1 and Sports Illustrated have him on their Week 2 running-back sit list. Green Bay beat writers expect Kaleb Johnson, who took zero offensive snaps in Week 1, to absorb work at the Jets. He projects 11.2 this week to Stafford's 17.4, so this does not cost you points even on the week. Everything else on your bench is protected: Tuten is the Lamar chip, Mayer is the Bowers hedge and is startable in this flex, Vele arrived 17 September and Allgeier arrived 18 September — both inside the seven-day churn window.

case.label: The second move, which nobody else will tell you about
case.body: Adding him is only half of it, and this is carried forward from yesterday's brief because it is the part that actually loses points. Jacksonville kick off at 14:05 Sunday and Los Angeles at 18:15 Monday. If Stafford is on the roster you must move Lawrence to the bench and Stafford into the QB slot BEFORE 14:05 Sunday, or Lawrence locks in at 14.9 and Stafford's 17.4 sits behind him all week. The add without the lineup change is worth nothing this week.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Another IPADE manager claims him off waivers before 01:00, which ends this at zero cost to you. Or Los Angeles put him on a report between now and Monday. If neither happens and the card is still unfired by 22 September, close it CHURN rather than carrying it a fourth run — that condition was written two runs ago and it stands.

action.label: Add Matthew Stafford · drop MarShawn Lloyd

whatWentWrong.title: The Lamar offer has been sent nine times and stops tonight
whatWentWrong.lead: The stop condition this brief wrote for itself — 'if both versions are declined by Friday, the read on that manager is wrong and the offer stops' — has fired. It is Friday night and Team 13 have never replied.

case.label: What was wrong
case.body: Not the trade. The read on the manager. This brief called the offer EVEN for three consecutive runs on someone who has never responded to anything, which is reporting the deal's merit as if it were his interest. Odds are a read on willingness, and nine unanswered messages is the only evidence of willingness that exists.

case.label: Why the trade row below survives anyway
case.body: The deal itself got better tonight, not worse — see the trade card. It stays visible as a standing offer because it costs nothing to leave on the table and because a run that deletes a good trade to look decisive has destroyed value here before. What stops is the Do-first card instructing you to send it again.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Team 13 opening the conversation themselves, or countering asking for Matthew Golden instead of Tuten — that version gains you more, and the standing instruction is to take it.

whatWentWrong.title: Your WR1 has an 8% target share and this brief has not said so until tonight
whatWentWrong.lead: Rashee Rice ran an 8% target share in Week 1, his lowest since Week 9 of his rookie season, and his slot rate fell from over 40% to 25%. He has been graded and started three runs running without that number appearing anywhere.

case.label: What is actually happening in Kansas City
case.body: Patrick Mahomes averaged 1.1 air yards per completion in Week 1, the lowest in the league, and went 0-for-4 on throws of ten or more yards. That is an offence throwing behind the sticks, and Rice being pushed out of the slot is the part that hurts in full PPR, where the slot is where receptions live.

case.label: Why he still starts
case.body: One game, and the alternative is worse: your bench receivers are Devaughn Vele against your own defence and nothing else. Kansas City are implied 27.0 at home. STRATEGY section 5 does not bench a top-ten receiver on one week of usage. This is a flag, not a move — but it should have been flagged on Wednesday.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A second week under 15% target share, or the slot rate staying at 25%. Two weeks of that is a role change and it makes him a sell-high candidate rather than an untouchable, which is a different brief entirely.

roster.footnote: Nothing has kicked off. Your earliest starter is Sunday at 11:00 and your last is Sunday night, so the right-hand column is the matchup read rather than a result. A dashed tile means I did not research that defence this run — absence, not a middling grade. One of your fourteen is dashed. Three more carry grades researched yesterday rather than tonight and each says so in its own tile.

starting.name: Trevor Lawrence
starting.detail: JAX · at DEN · SUN 14:05 · Jacksonville implied 21.0 against Denver's 23.5 — the only game on your card where your team is the underdog. He is your only quarterback until 01:00 tonight, and that is the whole argument for the card above. IF STAFFORD LANDS: move Lawrence to the bench and Stafford into the QB slot before 14:05 Sunday, or Lawrence locks in at 14.9 and Stafford's 17.4 sits behind him on Monday.
starting.gradeEvidence: DEN 29.8% missed-tackle rate in Week 1, third-worst since 2018 [carried from the 18 Sep 22:10Z run, not re-retrieved tonight]

Taylor took 88.7% of snaps and 95.7% of backfield touches, which is as much volume as exists — but he averages 12.3 points a game in losses and Alec Pierce is out, which thins the passing game that would keep this competitive.
starting.gradeEvidence: KC ranked 1st in run-defence success rate in Week 1

starting.name: Saquon Barkley
starting.detail: PHI · at TEN · SUN 11:00 · Jalen Hurts · Philadelphia implied 23.25 against Tennessee's 16.25, the lowest implied total on the entire Week 2 board. He is the game-script back STRATEGY section 5 wants and the 39.5 game total is the cap on it, which is why the tile is GOOD and not GREAT. 26 touches in the opener, and Philadelphia have talked publicly about managing that number.
starting.gradeEvidence: PHI -7, but 39.5 O/U is the lowest game total on your board

starting.name: Rashee Rice
starting.detail: KC · vs IND · SUN 18:20 · Patrick Mahomes · the bad news on your own player: an 8% target share in Week 1, his lowest since Week 9 of his rookie year, with his slot rate down from 40%+ to 25%. Mahomes averaged 1.1 air yards per completion, the league's lowest. The knee is off the injury report entirely and he plays. Kansas City implied 27.0.

starting.name: Garrett Wilson
starting.detail: NYJ · vs GB · SUN 11:00 · Geno Smith · Jets implied 20.5. Omar Cooper Jr. is out with an ankle, which thins the room again and concentrates targets on Wilson in a game Green Bay's front is expected to spend pressuring Smith — pressure produces quick throws, and quick throws in full PPR are receptions.

starting.name: Colston Loveland
starting.detail: CHI · vs MIN · SUN 11:00 · Caleb Williams · Chicago implied 27.5, the best environment on your roster. The role finding is now doubly sourced: Yahoo have him running a team-high 33 routes in Week 1 for zero catches, and yesterday's run found Bleacher Nation's tape review putting him on a route on all 27 Chicago pass plays, used deliberately as a decoy to pull coverage off Cole Kmet. The zero was scheme. The matchup is the problem: Minnesota allowed the fifth-fewest receiving yards to tight ends last season and held Green Bay's Tucker Kraft to 3 of 6 for 65 in Week 1. Four-target test resolves Sunday.
starting.gradeEvidence: MIN allowed the 5th-fewest receiving yards to tight ends last season

starting.name: Matthew Golden
starting.detail: GB · at NYJ · SUN 11:00 · Jordan Love · Green Bay implied 24.0, and the Jets are without safety Minkah Fitzpatrick with a strained groin. He keeps the flex over Michael Mayer by 0.9 of a point, which is inside the margin STRATEGY calls not worth moving for.

starting.name: Ravens D/ST
starting.detail: BAL · vs NO · SUN 11:00 · New Orleans implied 19.25. Acquired as a free agent with no priority spent. Baltimore sacked Daniel Jones twice on seventeen pressures in Week 1. Nothing on this wire is close — see the comparison in Do not chase.
starting.gradeEvidence: 3rd of 32 at FantasyPros; best available here is the Chargers at 10th

starting.detail: SEA · at ARI · SUN 14:25 · Seattle implied 23.0 as road favourites. Pro Football Network have him K9, behind Will Reichard at K5 and Chase McLaughlin at K6, both free agents here — and ESPN still projects Myers higher than either of them. The rankings and the projection disagree and the gap is under a point either way.

Brock Bowers is DOUBTFUL with the knee, Mayer led Las Vegas in receptions in Week 1 with six, and the Chargers let Trey McBride catch nine for 95 and a score in Week 1. trades.theirGainLine: Their gain is +2.5 this week and +40.6 across the season, against your +5.9 and +16.0 — more than twice yours on the season, and putting that number in the message is what gets it read.

case.label: New tonight, and it is the best version of this case yet
case.body: Team 13's second starting running back is Rachaad White. I researched him for the first time tonight for a different reason and the number is damning for them and perfect for this offer: 27 offensive snaps in his Commanders debut against Jacory Croskey-Merritt's 33, seven carries for 22 yards. He projects 7.6 and starts for them every week. Tuten projects 10.1. This is not a speculative upgrade for them, it is their weakest starting slot.

case.label: What it costs them
case.body: Nothing that plays. Lamar Jackson sits at slot 20 behind Josh Allen at slot 0 in a one-quarterback league — verified against tonight's snapshot, not assumed. He has scored them zero points and will score them zero points every week of the season. This is the structural surplus STRATEGY section 7 says to trade into.

case.label: What it gains you
case.body: Lawrence 14.9 to Jackson 20.8 is +5.9 this week and +16.0 on the season. NOT +30.9 — yesterday's run caught that error and corrected it, and I am not regressing it here: +30.9 is Lamar's season projection minus Lawrence's and forgets that Tuten leaves your season-projected flex. Read it with the Stafford card: if Stafford lands at 01:00 your quarterback floor becomes 17.4 and this trade's weekly gain falls to +3.4. Still worth making — Jackson is the better asset and Stafford becomes the hedge — but the two interact.

case.label: The honest risk
case.body: Nine offers, no reply, and I have now been wrong about this manager's willingness for three consecutive runs. The odds here are LONGSHOT and that is the ceiling. Separately, both season numbers rest on seasonProj, which has returned identical figures on every snapshot this week and may be a preseason artifact — the weekly numbers are the ones I would defend.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Team 13 acquire or start a second real running back, which kills their +40.6. Or they trade or drop a quarterback, which kills the surplus. Or Lamar Jackson appears on a Baltimore injury report — he is not on this week's, checked tonight. This row is not sent again as an instruction; it stays here so the deal is not lost if they ever answer.

trades.copyText: Hi — would you do Bhayshul Tuten for Lamar Jackson? You're carrying Lamar behind Josh Allen in a one-QB league, so he scores you nothing every week, and you're running three RBs for two slots. By my maths it's +40.6 season points for you against +16.0 for me. Tuten would start over Rachaad White, who managed 27 snaps and 22 rushing yards in Week 1. Happy to look at a different back on my side if Tuten isn't the one you want.

worthALook.name: T.J. Hockenson
worthALook.lead: The named replacement if the Loveland thesis breaks on Sunday, and the constraint is still the seat rather than the player.

case.label: The anomaly
case.body: 65% rostered nationally, free here, TE14 by rank. In a flex that takes a tight end, a second startable one has real value in this league in a way it does not in Chem.

case.label: What moved him, carried from yesterday
case.body: Minnesota ruled Kyler Murray out — confirmed again tonight, with Carson Wentz named starter — and Jauan Jennings is out too. Sports Illustrated moved Hockenson from TE23 to TE14 on that alone, reasoning that Wentz supports one receiver and a tight end rather than two receivers. He is Minnesota's number two target behind Jefferson on an 81% route share.

case.label: Why not tonight
case.body: Five bench seats hold the Lamar chip, tonight's Stafford drop, a tight end whose job depends on Bowers's knee, a receiver playing against your own defence and a back who arrived yesterday. After the Stafford add there are zero clean seats, not one.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Colston Loveland drawing fewer than four targets against Minnesota on Sunday. Two weeks of that is a role problem, at which point Hockenson takes the tight end slot and Loveland is the drop. As a free agent, never as a claim.

worthALook.name: Jake Ferguson
worthALook.lead: The largest ownership anomaly on this wire at 81.5% rostered and free, in the highest-total game of the week, and still declined for the fifth run on an unchanged reason.

case.label: The argument for him
case.body: Dallas carry a 27.0 implied total in the 50.5-point Washington game, the highest total on the Week 2 board. He is TE11 and nobody in a ten-team league should be able to have him for nothing.

case.label: The argument against, unchanged
case.body: Neither CeeDee Lamb nor George Pickens has appeared on a Dallas injury report, so he remains the third read in that passing game. A third read is not worth the last bench seat when that seat is about to hold your second quarterback.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Lamb or Pickens appearing on a Dallas injury report — Ferguson then becomes the best free agent in this league and the seat is his the same hour. Or Loveland failing the four-target test, in which case Hockenson and Ferguson are the same decision and Ferguson has the better game environment.

worthALook.name: Jakobi Meyers
worthALook.lead: 182.4 season projection, the highest of any receiver on this wire, free at 77% rostered, and held off for the same two reasons as yesterday.

case.label: Confirmed tonight
case.body: CBS report him limited at Friday's practice with the thumb and carrying no injury designation for Denver. A thumb on a receiver is a catch-rate injury and his ownership is falling 0.41 a day, which is the market selling the injury rather than buying the role.

case.label: The concentration problem
case.body: Bloodsports already hold Trevor Lawrence and Bhayshul Tuten from Jacksonville, and STRATEGY section 8 names a Week 7 Jaguars problem in this league specifically. A third Jaguar makes a scheduled hole worse.

case.label: When to act
case.body: If the Lamar trade lands, Tuten leaves and the Jacksonville concentration halves, which makes him a straightforward add on the freed seat. A clean Week 2 line with the thumb off the report does the same. A second week limited, or fewer than five targets at Denver, closes this row.

doNotChase.name: Will Reichard
doNotChase.lead: He is ranked two tiers above your kicker and he is free. You are not moving this seat, and here is the comparison rather than the omission.

case.label: The comparison, reported either way
case.body: Pro Football Network have Reichard K5 and Chase McLaughlin K6 against Jason Myers at K9. Both are free agents here, so no priority is at stake. Eddy Pineiro is K12, QUESTIONABLE, and on waivers clearing 07:00 on 20 September.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: ESPN projects Myers 9.4 this week against Reichard's 8.5 and McLaughlin's 8.7. The ranking and the projection disagree, the gap is under a point in both directions, and STRATEGY says not to propose a move worth under a point.

case.label: The rule that settles it
case.body: This seat changed hands at 07:06 yesterday when Cam Little became Jason Myers. Moving it again tonight would be the third kicker in four days — the exact rotating-bench-seat pattern STRATEGY section 3 exists to stop.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Myers finishing outside the top twenty kickers in Week 2 while Reichard or McLaughlin finish top five. The seat reopens on 22 September when the churn window expires, and the answer is whoever tops the board that week, as a free agent.

doNotChase.name: Chargers D/ST
doNotChase.lead: The best defence available in this league, reported so the hold on Baltimore is a decision rather than a silence.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: FantasyPros this week: Baltimore 3rd and 'start with confidence', Los Angeles 10th and 'matchup-dependent', Green Bay 9th, Cleveland 16th and on waivers. The Rams defence is 88.4% rostered and free here, which is the largest defensive ownership anomaly on the wire, and they are not in the top ten this week either.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Baltimore face New Orleans implied 19.25 and sacked Daniel Jones twice on seventeen pressures in Week 1. The Chargers face a Las Vegas team implied 18.25 — a similar draw behind a worse defence. Swapping 3rd for 10th is moving backwards for the cost of a transaction.

case.label: The standing rule
case.body: Never spend waiver priority on a defence in this league. That is absolute and it is not what is being tested here — both are free agents — but it is why the Browns defence on waivers is not even in this comparison.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Baltimore finishing outside the top twelve defensive scores in Week 2. The seat is then genuinely open on 23 September and the answer is whoever tops that week's board as a free agent.

doNotChase.name: Zach Charbonnet
doNotChase.lead: You added him Wednesday and dropped him Thursday. He is back on waivers and the price is now your entire season's priority.

case.label: What the claim would cost
case.body: He is on WAIVERS here clearing 07:00 on 20 September. One claim takes Bloodsports from 3rd of 10 to last for the rest of the season. That is the most expensive move available on this roster.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: A 0.0 projection. He is OUT with a shoulder described as indefinite, started the season on the PUP list, and no dated Seattle return timeline has been published across five runs of looking.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Seattle publishing a dated return and activating him — at which point he is a free agent again and can be re-added for nothing. Waiting dominates claiming in every branch. The only cost of waiting is another manager claiming an OUT running back, which nobody in this league has done all season.

doNotChase.name: Cam Little
doNotChase.lead: You dropped him at 07:06 on Thursday and he is K3 this week. Carried from yesterday because the trap has not expired: do not claim him back.

case.label: Why it looks right
case.body: Pro Football Network have Little K3 for Week 2 and Jason Myers K9. On merit the swap was a downgrade of six places and that is logged as a miss in Settled rather than defended.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: He clears waivers at 07:00 UTC on 20 September, so reaching him before Sunday's kickoffs requires a CLAIM. In IPADE that spends priority that never resets, on a kicker, which STRATEGY section 6 forbids by name. Six ranking places at kicker is worth about a point a week against a season's worth of priority.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing this week. If he is still unowned after Sunday he is a free agent and the comparison reopens at zero cost on 22 September, when this seat's churn window also expires.

settled.result: Held and paying. Bowers is DOUBTFUL with the knee, Mayer led Las Vegas in receptions in Week 1, and the Chargers allowed Trey McBride nine catches for 95 and a score.

settled.title: Hold Colston Loveland at tight end (16 September, unresolved for four runs)
settled.result: Held. A team-high 33 routes in Week 1 with zero catches is a role intact and a production question. The four-target test resolves Sunday.

settled.result: Held. Green Bay implied 24.0 and the Jets are without Minkah Fitzpatrick. Michael Mayer is the closer call now, at 0.9 of a point.

settled.result: Held and vindicated on the board: Baltimore 3rd this week, best available 10th.

settled.result: Held for a fifth run. Neither Lamb nor Pickens has appeared on a Dallas report, so the named trigger has not fired.

settled.result: Held. After tonight's Stafford add there are zero clean bench seats, which makes the seat argument stronger, not weaker.

settled.result: Held. Allen is Team 13's starting quarterback at slot 0, verified again against tonight's snapshot. STRATEGY section 7 names this exact failure mode.

settled.title: Hold Jason Myers rather than move the kicker seat a third time (18 September)
settled.result: Held, and the projection now agrees with the hold: Myers 9.4 against Reichard 8.5 and McLaughlin 8.7, even though the rankings do not.

settled.title: Decline a Zach Charbonnet waiver claim (18 September)
settled.result: Held. Still OUT, still no dated return, and the claim would still cost the season's priority.

cannotSee.label: Whether Stafford clears at 01:00 or is claimed first
cannotSee.body: Rivals' pending claims are invisible — ESPN only ever returns Bloodsports' own. Two other IPADE teams carry a second quarterback already and have no need of him; the rest have one each. If someone has a claim in, you find out at 01:00 and it costs you nothing, which is the whole reason the card says wait rather than claim.

cannotSee.label: This run fired at 22:35 Friday Mexico City, not 16:00
cannotSee.body: The schedule describes this as the 4:00 PM refresh with a morning run already published today. Neither matches: the previous brief was 22:12 UTC on 18 September, six hours ago, and it is Friday night here. Every deadline in this brief is computed from 04:14 UTC on 19 September. It also means this is not the Tuesday run — the weekly waiver batch clears 07:00 UTC on 23 September and the brief before that lock is still three days away.

cannotSee.label: One tile is dashed and three are borrowed from yesterday
cannotSee.body: Dashed: Tyler Allgeier — no Seattle defensive figure retrieved this run. Borrowed rather than re-researched: Trevor Lawrence and Bhayshul Tuten (Denver's Week 1 missed-tackle rate) and Devaughn Vele (Baltimore against slot receivers), all carried from the 18 September run and marked in their tiles. Rashee Rice's tile is graded on his own usage rather than on Indianapolis's coverage, which I did not research — so it tells you the offence is the problem without proving the opponent is not.

cannotSee.label: Whether KEI returns will set their lineup, which is the entire 77%
cannotSee.body: Four of their nine starting slots are empty and have been for three days, worth about 43 points. There is no way to see intent in a snapshot. Treat the 77% as provisional.

cannotSee.label: Brock Bowers's actual Sunday status
cannotSee.body: DOUBTFUL is roughly a 25% play rate and Pete Carroll has publicly left the door open. The inactive list publishes ninety minutes before kickoff. If Bowers plays, Mayer's tile is wrong and he is a bench body rather than your best reserve.

cannotSee.label: Season projections are frozen, which undercuts the trade arithmetic
cannotSee.body: seasonProj has returned identical figures on every snapshot this week. The +16.0 and +40.6 in the trade row are therefore August's opinion until proven otherwise, which is why the case leads with the weekly numbers and with Rachaad White's Week 1 snap count instead.

cannotSee.body: Trades are priced here on one week because only weekly projections are published and the season numbers are suspect. Season-long value is the right unit for a trade and this brief does not reliably have it.
